newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Tuesday in line with LME copper prices in the wake of a large build in LME warehouse copper stocks overnight.
COMEX September copper was called down 0.30 to 0.80 cent from Monday's finish of 112.15 cents a lb after trading from 112.45 to 110.50 cents on ACCESS.
LME copper stocks jumped 3,175 tonnes to 128,325 tonnes Tuesday, with 2,150 tonnes moving into the LME Singapore warehouse, probably from South Korea, traders said.
COMEX warehouse copper stocks fell 1,478 short tons to 46,270 short tons.
But the focus remains on Wednesday's LME July options declaration, and tightness in the cash-to-three month spread which was around $126.00 a tonne early Tuesday.
COMEX copper prices fell more than 10 cents early last week week, retreating from 12 month highs, before finding some support.
In industry news, Codelco's El Teniente mine in Chile has returned to usual output levels after being paralyzed by heavy snow storms for five days.
